cards.def: The coast-guard who watched the Geats' boat receives a gold-fitted sword, which makes him a respected man on the mead-bench.
Hygelac, king of the Geats, welcomes Beowulf home, hears his story, and rewards him with Hrethel's sword and land.
Hygelac says he had begged Beowulf not to go and wanted the Danes to settle their own feud with Grendel.
Hygd is Hygelac's young queen, daughter of Haereth, praised for her wisdom and generosity to the Geats.
Modthryth was a cruel queen who had any man who looked at her put to death, until her marriage to Offa softened her.
Offa is the famous king who married Modthryth and was honored far and wide for his generosity and fighting spirit.
Freawaru is Hrothgar's daughter, promised in marriage to Ingeld of the Heathobards to heal an old feud.
Ingeld is lord of the Heathobards, and Beowulf predicts that his love for Freawaru will cool once the feud with the Danes flares up again.
The Heathobards are Ingeld's people, who once lost a battle to the Danes and still resent the loot the Danes took.
In Beowulf's prediction, an old Heathobard sees a Dane wearing a looted sword and goads a young warrior into a killing that breaks the peace.
Handscio is the Geat warrior whom Grendel killed and ate first on the night of the fight.
Beowulf gives Hygelac the armor that belonged to Hrothgar's older brother Heorogar, which Heorogar never passed to his son Heoroweard.
Heoroweard is Heorogar's son, who never received his father's war-gear.
The Geats once thought young Beowulf a weakling who lacked force, a judgment his later deeds reversed.
Heardred is Hygelac's son, whom Beowulf guides until he is grown and who is killed by the Swedes for sheltering Ohthere's sons.
Onela is the Swedish king who kills Heardred, and Beowulf later avenges Heardred by helping Eadgils kill Onela.
Eanmund and Eadgils are Ohthere's sons, Swedish princes who rebelled against Onela and took refuge with the Geats.
Eadgils is the Swedish exile whom Beowulf supplies with men and weapons in the campaign that kills Onela.
The Shylfings are the Swedish royal line, the Geats' bitter enemies in a long series of feuds.
Ongentheow was the old Swedish king who killed Haethcyn at Ravenswood and was later killed by Eofor.
Eofor was Hygelac's warrior who killed Ongentheow and was rewarded with land, rings, and Hygelac's only daughter.
Wulf was Eofor's brother, wounded by Ongentheow just before Eofor killed the Swedish king.
Hrethel was Hygelac's father, who raised Beowulf and died of grief after one of his sons killed another by accident.
Herebeald was Hrethel's eldest son, killed by a stray arrow shot by his brother Haethcyn.
Haethcyn accidentally shot his brother Herebeald, then became king and was killed by Ongentheow at Ravenswood.
Dayraven was a Frankish standard-bearer whom Beowulf crushed to death with his bare hands.
The Hetware were a Frankish people who fought Hygelac on his fatal raid into Friesland.

cards.term: The Franks and the Merovingian king
cards.def: The messenger warns that the Franks and their Merovingian king have been the Geats' enemies ever since Hygelac's raid.
A runaway slave fleeing his master's punishment stumbled into the dragon's barrow and stole a gold cup to win back his master's favor.
The last survivor was the final member of a vanished noble race, who buried their treasure in the barrow and mourned until he died.
The dragon is a fire-breathing serpent that guards a buried hoard and burns the Geats' land after a cup is stolen.
Beowulf becomes king after Heardred's death and rules so strongly that no neighboring king dares to attack him.
Wiglaf is Beowulf's young kinsman and the only warrior who stays to help him fight the dragon.
Wiglaf is the son of Weohstan and the last of the Waegmundings, Beowulf's own clan.
Weohstan was Wiglaf's father, who killed Eanmund while serving Onela and passed Eanmund's sword and armor on to Wiglaf.
The Waegmundings are the clan of Beowulf and Wiglaf, which dies out with Beowulf.
Ten of Beowulf's chosen warriors fled to the woods during the dragon fight, and Wiglaf condemns them for disgracing their people.
A rider brings news of Beowulf's death to the waiting Geats and predicts wars with the Franks and the Swedes.

cards.term: The Geat woman at the pyre
cards.def: A Geat woman sings a lament at Beowulf's pyre, foretelling invasion, slaughter, and slavery for her people.
Hronesness is the headland where Beowulf asks to be buried in a barrow that sailors will see from the sea.
Earnaness is the place where the Geats find Beowulf's body lying beside the dead dragon.
Ravenswood is where Ongentheow killed Haethcyn and besieged the surviving Geats until Hygelac came to rescue them.
Friesland is the land of the Frisians, where Hygelac was killed on his raid.
